hints: Ask yourself what both prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells must do to survive: do both need to make proteins from DNA instructions?
Recall the three jobs in protein synthesis: copying DNA (mRNA), forming the ribosome (rRNA), and bringing amino acids (tRNA). Are any of these jobs skippable in either cell type?
walkthrough:
**Spot what both cells have in common**

Both prokaryotes (like bacteria) and eukaryotes (like plant and animal cells) make their own proteins. That means both must carry out transcription and translation.

Think: DNA -> RNA -> protein

**Match each RNA to its essential job**

mRNA carries the gene copy from DNA to the ribosome. rRNA builds the structure of the ribosome itself. tRNA brings the correct amino acids to the ribosome.

No cell can make protein without all three working together.

**Choose the row with all three present**

Since protein synthesis is universal, mRNA, rRNA and tRNA must all be found in both cell types. That is row A with three ticks.

options.A: Correct and reassuring. All three RNAs are essential for protein synthesis, which both prokaryotes and eukaryotes carry out.
options.B: Not quite. tRNA is not absent, both cell types need tRNA to deliver amino acids during translation.
options.C: Not quite. mRNA is not absent, both cell types need mRNA to carry the DNA code to ribosomes.
options.D: Not quite. Only rRNA is ticked here, but both cell types also need mRNA and tRNA to complete protein synthesis.
